sentences.text: Antliodus was an extinct genus of petalodonts, a group of cartilaginous fish belonging to the family Petalodontidae.
The genus is defined by its type species, Antliodus mucronatus, which serves as the primary reference for the group.
The genus Antliodus was described by Newberry and Worthen in 1866.
These animals lived between 346.7 and 298.9 million years ago, spanning from the Visean to the Gzhelian stages.
Fossils of Antliodus have been found in the Mississippian deposits of the United States, Britain, and Belgium.
